name: Material-Based Volumetric Emission
aliases: Volumetric Emission Displays, Fluorescent Volumetric Displays
text:
# Material-Based Volumetric Emission

Also called: Volumetric Emission Displays, Fluorescent Volumetric Displays

## Overview
Material-Based Volumetric Emission constructs 3D images by exciting luminescent materials (fluorescent inks or doped glass) to emit visible light directly from within a volume [S1, S2, unofficial]. It solves the lack of natural ocular accommodation in 2D displays by creating physical light sources at arbitrary depths [S1, unofficial]. It differs from scanning methods like [Galvanometer Scanner Volume Rendering](5277-galvanometer-scanner-volume-rendering.md) by using static or semi-static material structures that emit light upon excitation, rather than scanning a single point of light through empty space [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The family relies on the conversion of excitation energy (typically UV or infrared lasers) into visible light emission within a volumetric medium.

1.  **Excitation Mechanism**:
    *   **Fluorescence/Upconversion**: Materials absorb high-energy photons (e.g., UV at 365 nm [S1, unofficial] or IR at 800/1550 nm [S2, unofficial]) and re-emit lower-energy visible photons.
    *   **Two-Photon Absorption**: In rare-earth doped glass, two infrared photons are absorbed simultaneously to excite an ion to a higher energy state, which then relaxes by emitting a visible photon [S1, S2, unofficial]. This process is non-linear, occurring only at the intersection of high-intensity beams [S1, unofficial].

2.  **Voxel Definition**:
    *   A voxel is a physical location within the medium where emission occurs.
    *   In inkjet methods, voxels are discrete layers of printed dye [S1, unofficial].
    *   In glass methods, voxels are defined by the spatial intersection of scanning beams within doped layers [S1, unofficial].

3.  **Color Generation**:
    *   Color is determined by the specific luminescent material (dye or dopant) at the voxel location [S1, S2, unofficial].
    *   Red: Europium complex [S1, unofficial] or Praseodymium (Pr) [S2, unofficial].
    *   Green: $\beta$-quinophthalone [S1, unofficial] or Erbium (Er) [S2, unofficial].
    *   Blue: Coumarin dyes [S1, unofficial] or Thulium (Tm) [S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Inkjet Printing-Based Volumetric Display](6810-inkjet-printing-based-volumetric-display.md)
Constructs a static volume by printing fluorescent inks onto stacked transparent films. It uses a [multi-view projection](#5937-multi-view-projection.md) algorithm to determine ink density such that superimposed emission matches target patterns from specific angles. Choose this for full-color, static 3D images with motion parallax using commercial printing hardware.

### [Downing Three-Color Display](7247-downing-three-color-display.md)
Generates true 3D images in a static glass medium using two intersecting infrared laser beams to trigger upconversion in rare-earth doped layers. Choose this for viewing from any angle without mechanical movement of the display material, leveraging optical addressing rather than physical layering.

### Kumagai Fluorescent Polymer Screen
A method using a screen with a laminated structure of fluorescent polymer or pixel structure to draw color volumetric images with fluorescent voxels. It adopts computer holograms for light irradiation pattern control, improving [voxel count](#2908-grid-resolution-calculation.md) and brightness [S1, unofficial].

### Translucent Helix Rear-Projection Diffusion
Rear-projection volumetric display using a translucent plastic helix where laser light is projected from below, diffused through the material, and visible from above and below, eliminating overhead mirrors [S2, unofficial].
*   **Intensity Balancing**: Adjust material properties so light reflected from the bottom surface and transmitted through the top surface have equal intensity, minimizing brightness discontinuity when viewing angle crosses the helical blade plane [S2, unofficial].
*   **Parameters**: Test material: 0.020-inch-thick high-impact polystyrene. Vacuum-formed into two identical blades, bonded along central axis, mounted in closed cylindrical housing [S2, unofficial]. Drive system for translucent model: 1-inch diameter, 2.5-inch-long vertical shaft extension directly driven by 1/10-hp DC motor. Two mirrors fold projected laser signal upward [S2, unofficial].

## Background
Originated from research into volumetric displays using luminescent materials. Early work included upconversion nanoparticles [S1, unofficial]. The family includes methods using fluorescent polymer screens [S1, unofficial] and translucent helical structures for transportable systems [S2, unofficial]. It is used in applications requiring true 3D visualization with natural accommodation, such as medical imaging or interactive displays.
